newsitem.title: FRANCE: Portugal's IGCP says comfortable with lower rates.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's IGCP says comfortable with lower rates.

text.p: Portugal's Institute for Public Credit Management (IGCP) on Wednesday said it would be comfortable with lower interest rates but had grown used to the caution of the Portuguese central bank.

"The Bank of Portugal traditionally is cautious. Of course from a treasury point of view we would be comfortable with interest rates lower but we have to admit that the Bank...has a long experience in managing the currency and monetary policy," executive director Vasco Pereira told Reuters at a Paris conference.
"Traditionally they are cautious so it's nothing new for us," he said.

Portugal rejected all the bids at a three-month Treasury bill sale on Wednesday and promptly issued a 10 billion yen dual-currency bond as it could obtain better conditions than those offered by the local market, according to IGCP president Vitor Bento.
Analysts in Portugal said the move was a clear signal that the IGCP expects domestic interest rates to fall.

Pereira said there were several reasons why the IGCP might reject bids at a Treasury bill sale. He said it could be a function of the Treasury's needs but sometimes, if interest rates were not considered low enough, it rejected bids.
"Every month we announce the issues we are going to have next month...sometimes our Treasury does not follow exactly the needs we are forecasting for," Pereira said.

Asked whether IGCP rejected bids if interest rates were not low enough he said, "Sometimes it happens also...if there's a shortage of liquidity in the market that makes bids (that) are not suitable as they should be for us.
"That does not change our commitment to keep the debts clear and it happens from time to time that we just don't issue but its very rare," he said.
The last six-month and 12-month Treasury bills sold in Portugal were at 5.3445 percent and 5.2823, respectively, against 5.001 and 4.960 in Spain.
The Bank of Portugal repo rate stands at 5.70 percent against 5.25 percent in Spain.
